Your brief, translated

Ground and first floors each have two bedrooms with private attached bathrooms, a separate kitchen, a furnished TV lounge, open dining area and a 6.5 ft clear bedroom gallery and an aligned stair. The basement brings the social lounge, cinema, study, prayer room and an additional bathroom together. Upstairs, the car-bay footprint becomes a shaded balcony.

Five different floor plans

Design 1 has two rear bedrooms and a front kitchen. Design 2 moves one bedroom to the centre, the kitchen to the left and an ensuite forward on the right. Design 3 places both bedrooms farther forward, with bathrooms behind them and a left galley kitchen. Design 4 moves the kitchen across the rear centre, enlarges the rear bathrooms and gives the TV lounge the full front width. Design 5 places bedrooms on opposite sides, merges the TV lounge and dining, and separates the enlarged rear kitchen behind a screened lobby and a solid privacy door. Both main floors use the same wet-area positions within each option.

Dimensions & practical planning

  • The assumed square plot remains 1,836 sq ft, approximately 42.85 ft per side. The main building envelope remains 42.5 × 32 ft.
  • Each main floor has two bedrooms of at least 162.5 sq ft, each with a direct private bathroom. Bathroom proportions and locations change across the five options.
  • Every option retains a 6.5 ft clear passage, running across or along the house according to the plan. Kitchens, dining rooms and TV lounges move with the walls and doors.
  • The rear garden strip remains removed. Designs 3 and 4 move the car bay forward into the front courtyard, within the same boundary. The main vehicle gate, separate pedestrian gate and house entrance stay in place.
  • The central bedroom in Design 2 requires a professionally designed daylight and ventilation solution; room windows and any lightwell must be resolved for the actual site.

Services and access

The main stair remains aligned on every level. Plumbing must be redesigned for the chosen option. Kitchen extract, bathroom ventilation, and a replacement compliant basement escape route remain part of the architect’s work. Roof, boundary and gates stay fixed while internal plans change.

Before construction

This is a concept to develop with a local architect and structural engineer, not an approved construction or structural plan. Confirm the real survey, boundary walls, road level, scheme-specific setbacks, allowable use, FAR and services. The basement needs soil and groundwater checks, engineered retaining walls, excavation support, waterproofing, ventilation, drainage and pumped sewage. Verify escape design, stair headroom, structure, seismic design and roof loads. Prayer direction is illustrative and must be set for the actual site.

Reference checked: PDA Building Control Regulations 2024 ↗. Applicable authority and plot conditions remain unconfirmed. This is one family home with two kitchens, not two approved independent units.
